query: What operational burdens appear in incident descriptions?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Describes the type/domain of the incident (database, email, VPN), not an aspect of the burden it imposes. It classifies what broke, which is a predictor of burden, not a part of it.

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Captures the nature of the failure (connectivity, access denied, outage). This characterizes the fault, not the operational burden as an aspect; it is a driver of burden rather than a constitutive part.

per_column.name: affected_resource_scope
per_column.rationale: Where the burden falls (server-side, network, client-side) is a genuine dimension of operational burden -- which part of the operation must be engaged. Borderline but part-of the burden's locus.

per_column.name: incident_blast_radius
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact (individual vs system-wide vs location) is a constitutive aspect of how large the operational burden is -- an impact-magnitude facet.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident resolved without intervention directly speaks to the effort/handling burden -- a facet of the operational load actually incurred.

per_column.name: recurrent_caller
per_column.rationale: A property of the caller, not an aspect of the burden. It may correlate with burden but is not a constitutive part of it.

per_column.name: off_hours_incident
per_column.rationale: Timing (off-hours) is a facet of operational burden because it modulates the cost/effort of handling -- a temporal-load aspect of the burden.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Recurrence is a genuine aspect of ongoing operational burden (repeated work), though it overlaps heavily with recurrent_caller in intent.

judge.rationale: Only a subset of the added columns are true meronymic facets of operational_burden. incident_category and failure_symptom describe what/how the incident failed -- external predictors that classify the fault rather than aspects of the burden itself. recurrent_caller is a caller attribute. Among the facet-like columns, recurrence_signal and recurrent_caller substantially overlap (both encode recurrence), and off_hours_incident, blast_radius, and self_resolved each touch different aspects but overlap loosely on 'handling effort', lowering mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the set touches impact scope, locus, timing, resolution effort, and recurrence, but omits central burden dimensions such as time-to-resolve / effort-hours, staffing/escalation cost, SLA/priority pressure, and reopen/backlog load. As a whole the column set leans toward classifying incidents rather than cleanly decomposing the burden concept into MECE constitutive parts.
